terms.gloss: take revenge on, punish, get even with
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, deponent: aliquem (the person), or aliquid (the wrong); prō with the ablative of the wrong
evidence: Cic. Att. 9.12.2: ōdī hominem et ōderō: utinam ulcīscī possem! (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 1.14: aliquem prō scelere (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The person punished is the direct object: ulcīscī aliquem prō factīs ejus, to get even with someone for what he did. Lewis & Short: “very freq. and class.”

phrases.latin: Utinam istum ulcīscī possem prō factīs ejus!
phrases.english: If only I could get even with him for what he did!

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 99, checked against the searchable text and the page image (12 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
